# Release 1.1.0 research

## Reused evidence

Reuse the inspected 17-commit history from tag `1.0.0` to `8b099f9` and the
CLI-version qualification record rather than repeat runtime research.
No new runtime features are required for this release.

* The default project version remains `1.0.0`
  (`src/wharf/wharf.csproj:9`); there is no 1.0.1 tag.
* README already documents HydraFusion, provider-selected effort, single-dash
  concurrency flags, and removed double-dash spellings (`README.md:7-17`).
* CLI boundary tests cover the new aliases and rejected former concurrency
  options (`tests/wharf.Tests/WharfAppTests.cs:13-56`).
* Existing qualification checks format, Release build/tests, secret patterns,
  Debian packaging, checksums, and SBOM (`scripts/qualify-release.sh:15-44`).
* Existing CLI image-version qualification passed tests and Docker smoke
  (`.github/tracking/2026-10-15-cli-version-image-resolution-review.md:16-23`).
* Named tmux foreground execution and read-only capture are the monitoring
  contract (`../deep-swe/RUN_MONITORING.md:15-34`).

## Recommendation and boundaries

Release the accumulated changes as user-approved 1.1.0. Explicitly document
removed CLI spellings and changed defaults; do not describe the release as
fully backward-compatible. Keep historical qualification and benchmark
records unchanged. Use the existing qualification script plus a fresh .NET
Docker smoke, retain evidence, verify version output, then push a 1.1.0
branch and tag. Git transport works; GitHub CLI authentication is unavailable,
so a hosted GitHub Release is not currently publishable through that CLI.

No new benchmarks, features, host changes, multi-host qualification, or
changes to scoring are included.

## Release-blocking discovery

The package script copies only the .NET apphost, not its DLL, runtime
configuration, or dependencies (`scripts/package-wharf.sh:21-22`).
Executing the extracted package exits 154 with
`The application to execute does not exist: .../usr/lib/wharf/wharf.dll`.
Existing packaging tests inspect script text only
(`tests/wharf.Tests/PackagingScriptTests.cs:6-19`), so checksum and metadata
checks did not detect the unusable payload.

Recommendation: copy the complete publish output, add an extracted-package
execution regression test, and make qualification run the packaged version
command. This is a release-blocking packaging correction, not new runtime
scope. Retain the failed package separately from the replacement.
